statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study paired mutations from 5,120 whole-genome-sequenced tumors, spanning 40 cancer types, with 516 topographical genomic features drawn from ENCODE.
statements.evidence: we integrate mutations from 5,120 whole-genome-sequenced tumors from 40 cancer types with 516 topographical features from ENCODE
statements.note: The abstract states that mutations from 5,120 whole-genome-sequenced tumors of 40 cancer types were integrated with 516 ENCODE topographical features.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Of all the topographical features examined, replication timing had the strongest influence on the accumulation of mutational signatures.
statements.evidence: to evaluate the effect of nucleosome occupancy, histone modifications, CTCF binding, replication timing, and transcription/replication strand asymmetries on the cancer-specific accumulation of mutations from distinct mutagenic processes
statements.note: Replication timing is listed among the features evaluated, but the abstract never ranks the features by the size of their effect.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most mutational signatures were influenced by topographical features, and signatures sharing related etiologies responded to them in similar ways.
statements.evidence: Most mutational signatures are affected by topographical features, with signatures of related etiologies being similarly affected.
statements.note: The abstract reports that most signatures are affected by topographical features and that signatures of related etiologies are affected similarly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Near topographical features, some signatures displayed periodic patterns or were enriched or depleted in a manner specific to the cancer type.
statements.evidence: Certain signatures exhibit periodic behaviors or cancer-type-specific enrichments/depletions near topographical features
statements.note: The abstract states that certain signatures show periodic behaviour or cancer-type-specific enrichments and depletions near topographical features.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The additional blood-cell mutations caused by chemotherapy increased the treated individuals' risk of developing therapy-related leukemia.
statements.evidence: The results show the long-term biological consequences of cytotoxic agents to which a substantial fraction of the population is exposed as part of disease management
statements.note: The abstract describes long-term biological consequences of chemotherapy in blood cells but reports no data on subsequent leukemia risk.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Some chemotherapeutic agents imposed substantially higher somatic mutation loads on blood cells, although the effect varied with the drug and the blood cell type.
statements.evidence: Substantial additional somatic mutation loads with characteristic mutational signatures were imposed by some chemotherapeutic agents, but the effects were dependent on the drug and blood cell types.
statements.note: The abstract reports substantial additional mutation loads from some chemotherapeutic agents, with effects that depended on drug and blood cell type.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Blood cell genomes were sequenced from 23 chemotherapy-treated individuals whose ages ranged from 3 to 80 years.
statements.evidence: we sequenced blood cell genomes from 23 individuals aged 3-80 years who were treated with a range of chemotherapy regimens
statements.note: The abstract states that blood cell genomes were sequenced from 23 chemotherapy-treated individuals aged 3 to 80 years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Chemotherapy prematurely altered the cell population structure of normal blood, producing changes resembling those that come with normal aging.
statements.evidence: Chemotherapy induced premature changes in the cell population structure of normal blood, similar to those caused by normal aging.
statements.note: The abstract states that chemotherapy induced premature, aging-like changes in the cell population structure of normal blood.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The common amplified region of chromosome 21 spanned 7.8 Mb and contained 71 genes, 43 of them differentially expressed relative to non-iAMP21-ALL cases.
statements.evidence: a 7.8 Mb common region of amplification harboring 71 genes, 43 of which were differentially expressed compared with non-iAMP21-ALL ones
statements.note: The abstract delineates a 7.8 Mb common region of amplification with 71 genes, 43 of which were differentially expressed versus non-iAMP21-ALL.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell genomic profiling exposed clonal heterogeneity and placed acquisition of the iAMP21 chromosome at an early point in disease development.
statements.evidence: we documented clonal heterogeneity and genomic evolution, demonstrating that the acquisition of the iAMP21 chromosome is an early event
statements.note: The abstract reports that single-cell profiling documented clonal heterogeneity and showed acquisition of the iAMP21 chromosome to be an early event.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Among iAMP21-ALL patients, those whose leukemia arose with a constitutional chromosomal aberration had worse survival than the others.
statements.evidence: including rare cases arising in the context of constitutional chromosomal aberrations
statements.note: The abstract mentions that such rare cases were included in the cohort but reports no survival comparison for them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Characteristic secondary genetic features of iAMP21-ALL included an elevated mutation load and UV mutational signatures.
statements.evidence: We show that UV-mutational signatures and high mutation load are characteristic secondary genetic features.
statements.note: The abstract names UV-mutational signatures and high mutation load as characteristic secondary genetic features of iAMP21-ALL.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study analysed whole-genome sequences of tumors from 22 patients carrying germline TP53 pathogenic variants.
statements.evidence: Here, we perform whole-genome sequence (WGS) analysis of tumors from 22 patients with TP53 germline pathogenic variants.
statements.note: The abstract states that tumors from 22 patients with germline TP53 pathogenic variants underwent whole-genome sequencing.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LFS tumors acquired TP53 LOH, accompanied by mutant-allele amplification, earlier than tumors carrying somatic TP53 mutations did.
statements.evidence: We identify near-ubiquitous early loss of heterozygosity of TP53, with gain of the mutant allele. This occurs earlier in these tumors compared to tumors with somatic TP53 mutations
statements.note: The abstract reports that TP53 loss of heterozygosity with mutant-allele gain occurs earlier in LFS tumors than in tumors with somatic TP53 mutations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Somatic mutations in homologous recombination genes made LFS tumors sensitive to PARP inhibitors.
statements.evidence: We observe somatic mutations affecting Wnt, PI3K/AKT signaling, epigenetic modifiers and homologous recombination genes
statements.note: The abstract reports somatic mutations in homologous recombination genes but gives no data on PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Phylogenetic trees built from bulk and multi-region whole-genome sequencing showed comparatively little heterogeneity within LFS tumors.
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic trees of tumor evolution, reconstructed from bulk and multi-region WGS, reveal that LFS tumors exhibit comparatively limited heterogeneity.
statements.note: The abstract states that phylogenetic reconstruction revealed comparatively limited heterogeneity in LFS tumors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among lung cancer patients with AFR ancestry, KRAS mutations were rarer regardless of smoking status, while the TP53 association with AFR ancestry appeared in smokers alone.
statements.evidence: in lung cancer, KRAS mutations are less common in both smokers and non-smokers with AFR ancestry, whereas the association of TP53 mutations with AFR ancestry is only seen in smokers
statements.note: The abstract reports less common KRAS mutations with AFR ancestry in both smokers and non-smokers, and a TP53 association seen only in smokers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In lung, breast and prostate cancers, three of the six cancer types studied, MYC amplification was enriched among patients with AFR ancestry.
statements.evidence: AFR ancestry in six common cancers. Cross-cancer type associations, such as an enrichment of MYC amplification with AFR ancestry in lung, breast, and prostate cancers
statements.note: The abstract reports enrichment of MYC amplification with AFR ancestry in lung, breast and prostate cancers, three of the six cancers studied.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In lung cancers, AFR ancestry was linked to fewer KRAS G12C and EGFR L858R alterations but to more frequent ROS1 fusions.
statements.evidence: such as depletion of KRAS G12C and EGFR L858R, and enrichment of ROS1 fusion with AFR ancestry in lung cancers
statements.note: The abstract lists depletion of KRAS G12C and EGFR L858R and enrichment of ROS1 fusion with AFR ancestry among actionable alterations in lung cancer.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Tumors from patients with AFR ancestry had a higher overall tumor mutational burden than tumors from patients of other ancestries.
statements.evidence: We leverage two large genomic cohorts to investigate the relationship between genomic alterations and AFR ancestry in six common cancers.
statements.note: The abstract reports enrichment or depletion of specific alterations with AFR ancestry but makes no comparison of overall mutational burden.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Breast and gynecologic cancers were enriched for multi-PIK3CA mutations, which occurred in 11% of all PIK3CA-mutant tumors.
statements.evidence: Multi-PIK3CA mutations are found in 11% of all PIK3CA-mutant tumors, including 9% of low tumor mutational burden (TMB) PIK3CA-mutant tumors, and are enriched in breast and gynecologic cancers.
statements.note: The abstract reports multi-PIK3CA mutations in 11% of PIK3CA-mutant tumors, with enrichment in breast and gynecologic cancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumors with multi-PIK3CA mutations tended to lack mutations in other driver genes and in other PI3K pathway genes.
statements.evidence: These mutations tend to be mutually exclusive of mutations in other driver genes, and of genes in the PI3K pathway.
statements.note: The abstract states that multi-PIK3CA mutations tend to be mutually exclusive with mutations in other driver genes and PI3K pathway genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, multi-PIK3CA mutant tumors responded better to PI3K inhibition than tumors with a single PIK3CA mutation.
statements.evidence: patients with different classes of multi-PIK3CA mutant estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancers respond similarly to PI3K inhibition
statements.note: The abstract compares PI3K-inhibitor response only across classes of multi-PIK3CA mutant breast cancers, not against single-mutant tumors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Multi-PIK3CA mutations were found in 18% of high-TMB PIK3CA-mutant tumors, which often showed an APOBEC mutational signature.
statements.evidence: Among PIK3CA-mutant tumors with a high TMB, 18% are multi-PIK3CA mutant and often harbor an apolipoprotein B mRNA-editing enzyme, catalytic polypeptide (APOBEC) mutational signature.
statements.note: The abstract reports that 18% of high-TMB PIK3CA-mutant tumors are multi-PIK3CA mutant and often carry an APOBEC signature.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.note: The abstract describes what CELLO2 was built to forecast but reports no accuracy comparison with grade-based models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study examined sequencing and clinical data from initial and recurrent tumor pairs of 544 adult diffuse gliomas.
statements.evidence: we collected sequencing and clinical data of initial-recurrent tumor pairs from 544 adult diffuse gliomas
statements.note: The abstract states that sequencing and clinical data were collected from initial-recurrent tumor pairs of 544 adult diffuse gliomas.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In IDH-wild-type glioma, Ki67 expression at initial diagnosis correlated positively with the tumor becoming hypermutated by recurrence.
statements.evidence: Ki67 expression at diagnosis was positively correlated with acquiring hypermutation at recurrence in the IDH-wild-type glioma.
statements.note: The abstract reports a positive correlation between Ki67 expression at diagnosis and hypermutation at recurrence in IDH-wild-type glioma.

statements.label: supported

statements.evidence: demonstrated that MYC drives temozolomide resistance by promoting hypermutation
statements.note: The abstract states that temozolomide-induction experiments demonstrated that MYC drives temozolomide resistance by promoting hypermutation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Countries with higher HNC incidence also had greater mutation burdens from tobacco-associated signatures.
statements.evidence: Differences in HNC incidence between countries corresponded with differences in mutation burdens of tobacco-associated signatures, consistent with the dominant role of tobacco in HNC causation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that between-country differences in HNC incidence corresponded with tobacco-signature mutation burdens, consistent with tobacco's dominant causal role.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tobacco smoking was linked to altered mutational spectra, a different repertoire of cancer-gene driver mutations and distinct copy number change patterns.

statements.note: The abstract states that tobacco smoking was associated with differences in mutational spectra, driver mutation repertoire and copy number change patterns.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The HNC genomes revealed six tobacco-associated mutational signatures, some of which were new.
